title: 1. Identify which state feedback the qualified expert needs
hypothesis: Instantaneous pen-state feedback is necessary for the PPO expert to retain the pen, even when hand proprioception and action history remain available.

prediction.rationale: Baseline is the unmodified qualified Stage-3 PPO expert; clamping pen-state observations should reduce sustained success by at least 0.30, identifying feedback information that symbolic repair must preserve.

protocol.command: gpu run bash -lc 'source ~/IsaacLab/source_env.sh && python scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py --config config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml --study feedback_lesions --stage 3 --seed 4140 --cases 40 --arms expert,expert_repeat,pen_state_clamped,hand_state_clamped --manifest config/manifests/pen_spin_feedback_lesions_s4140.yaml'
code_changes: Extend scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py with the displayed study arguments; resolve the frozen D-036 qualified PPO checkpoint and record its hash.

Clamp selected named observation fields to their episode-initial values before policy inference, including redundant encodings of the selected state; leave the simulator unmodified and retain valid quaternion representations.
Run full expert, repeated full expert, pen-state clamp and hand-proprioception clamp in separate Isaac processes on identical placements; use the frozen sustained-success reducer.
Freeze the new 40-case diagnostic manifest before rollout. Gate interpretation on zero repeated-control outcome flips and at most 4/40 diverged trajectories.
Document that D-037 removed all feedback through action replay, whereas this intervention retains the policy and other feedback channels; necessity does not establish sufficiency.

falsified_by: The paired interval for pen-clamped minus baseline success lies entirely above -0.30. An interval containing zero is not evidence that pen feedback matters.
direction: Continue researching the single-step exploration pipeline with plateau-triggered trace repair, extended to pen spinning on the Shadow Hand (Isaac Lab Isaac-ShadowHandSpin-Stage{1,2,3}-Direct-v0, vendored in lares/envs/isaac_pen_spin; 157-d full obs, 20-d action, 60 Hz, 360-step episodes). Expert demonstrations: first try a hand-written scripted spinning controller; also search online for an existing trained pen-spinning policy; if neither qualifies, train an RL expert (rsl_rl PPO on the box). No budget ceiling on GPU hours or LLM calls. Known gaps to turn into questions: the env's spin_rate is roll about the pen's own long axis (not end-over-end twirl), success is per step with no episode rule, and the pipeline (manifests, obs schema, runner, records) is MetaWorld-only today. Debug issues, improve the pipeline, and turn unexpected findings into concrete research questions; document results and limitations.

advisor.reasoning: This cheaply localizes the qualified checkpoint's dependence on feedback channels, unlike D-037's removal of all feedback. However, clamping creates distribution shift, and sustained-success loss does not distinguish dropping the pen from failing the spin threshold. Narrow the hypothesis rather than interpreting this intervention as proof that pen-state information is necessary for retention; the budget remains 160 episodes and zero LLM calls.
suggested_changes: Replace the hypothesis with: 'The qualified PPO checkpoint relies on changing pen-state observations to maintain sustained axial-roll success when hand proprioception and action history remain available.'

Keep the prediction as paired_success_difference, decrease by at least 0.30 against the unmodified qualified expert, using the frozen sustained-success reducer. Keep falsified_by as an interval entirely above -0.30; an interval including zero establishes no difference.

Reuse scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py and config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml on seed 4140. Use existing per-step traces to separate drops from tail-spin failures, and explicitly limit conclusions to this checkpoint's dependence under clamping—not information-theoretic necessity or feedback sufficiency.

implementer.reasoning: Agree with all three changes. Clamping is a distribution-shift intervention, so the conclusion must be limited to this checkpoint's dependence under clamping; reporting drops versus tail-spin failures from the existing per-step traces is what makes the result useful to a repair packet. Implementation note: clamp = hold the named observation slice at its value from the case's reset observation for the whole episode, each arm one fresh Isaac process (D-034/D-035), cases from seed 4140 (unused).
